_readme: Every playable character. Edit this file, then run Prince's Palace > Build Default Content. id is written into save files, so never rename one after a save exists; role and attackType are matched case-insensitively against CharacterRole and DamageType, and CharacterEntryResolver rejects an unknown name at build time rather than shipping a character that silently falls through to the wrong Skill case. THE SIX ABILITY SCORES NO LONGER FOLLOW A FIXED BUDGET. Through 2026-09-07 every character's six scores had to total exactly 60, so differentiation was redistribution rather than growth: a new character could not be quietly stronger than the roster by being above average at everything, because to be tough somewhere it had to be feeble somewhere else. The owner dropped that rule on 2026-09-07 and shipped Shawn/Bjorn/Odette at totals of 66/64/62 as written, on the reasoning that the three authored spreads read fine without it; CharacterEntryResolver and ContentDatabase.ValidateContent no longer refuse an off-total row. If a future character turns out to be a flatly stronger pick than the roster for having no real weakness, that is the failure mode the budget existed to prevent, and reinstating `total == AbilityScoreBudget` in both places (the constant is gone; it was 60, six times the neutral score) is the fix. Each score still has to be a plausible number on its own — refused below 1 or above 30 in the resolver, and outside 3-20 in the built-catalogue check. STAT SPREADS EXPRESS THE ROLE, so a squad's strengths are readable from its species alone, and attackType gives each character an elemental identity for the weakness/resistance system: three characters cover three of the six DamageType values, chosen by loose theme (wool/pasture, brute strength, old and wise) rather than min-maxed against the enemy roster. BOTH ART PATHS ARE RESOURCES-RELATIVE AND CARRY NO EXTENSION: portraitPath names one head-and-shoulders PNG under Resources/Portraits/ (the dossier plate) and battleSpritePath a folder of full-body stance art (the fight stage, produced by tools/slice_actor_sheet.py). Both load at runtime, so a row added here is complete the moment the content is rebuilt. portraitPath was ASSETS-relative and baked into the scene until 2026-09-06, which meant a character authored between scene builds had a correct name, correct attributes and an empty portrait plate that no content rebuild could fill; the two conventions still coexist elsewhere in content (iconPath, iconSheet are baked), and ArtPathConvention is the one statement of which field is which. owl now wears her own portrait (Portraits/owl), drawn 2026-09-19. SIGNATURE RESOURCES are each character's own private combat resource; an EMPTY signatureId means the character has none — that is the meaningful distinction, not a zero capacity. WHICH POOL A CHARACTER'S SKILLS SPEND IS ALSO CONTENT: primaryPoolId names a row in pools.json and blank means mana, so trading mana for a different resource — a different capacity rule, different gains, different colours, and no spell books — is one field on this row rather than a special case in code (Bjorn's is `fury`). A signature resource rides the same three triggers (per-turn, on-attack, on-damage-taken), so a new one is content and wiring rather than a parallel system. Wool (Shawn) is the only one shipped today, and it is PER-TURN-LED AT BASE: the row authors signatureGainPerTurn 1 and nothing else — signatureGainOnAttack and signatureGainOnDamageTaken are both 0, so a base Shawn banks exactly one wool a turn no matter what he does with it. That is the floor, not the ceiling, and the two things that raise it are both content rather than code. The reward track grows the resource itself: sheep's milestones pay SignatureGainPerTurn at 10 and again at 50, SignatureCapacity at 25 and 100, SignatureGainOnDamageTaken at 40, with twelve more capacity spread through the filler — so income and capacity are both a function of level, and a level-100 Shawn is a different economy from a level-1 one. Talents add OTHER income on top: swearing to the Black Ram (sheep_ram_root) turns being hit into wool (WoolOnHitTaken) and pays more per turn the worse the day is going (WoolPerTurnBelowHealth at 67% and 33% health), which is how a damage-taken engine reaches him at all. This paragraph used to call Wool attack-led and claim his plain Attack paid the most; it never did, on any commit of this tree (AUDIT #127). ABOUT THE OTHER HALF OF the old ‘armour and ammunition’ line: wool does NOT absorb damage today. The row authors signatureAbsorbsDamage false, so ResourcePool.Absorb returns 0 and incoming damage goes straight to his health; wool is ammunition only until the track's SignatureAbsorbs reward at level 60 switches the armour half on, and from there the bank-or-spend tension is real for the rest of the character's life. Whether level 60 is the right place to hand that over, or whether the base row should ship absorbing, is still open (AUDIT #121). He starts every fight at zero, which is why he has the worst opening turn in the game and the best closing one. Bjorn spends fury instead, a pool rather than a signature (primaryPoolId, not signatureId, so none of the three signature triggers apply to it); Odette carries neither and spends plain mana. ALL THREE STARTING SPREADS ARE AUTHORED NOW, as of 2026-09-07: Shawn (STR 12, DEX 10, CON 14, WIS 12, INT 8, CHA 10 — total 66), Bjorn (STR 12, DEX 12, CON 14, WIS 8, INT 8, CHA 10 — total 64) and Odette (STR 8, DEX 12, CON 8, WIS 12, INT 14, CHA 8 — total 62), each shipped as written on the owner's call rather than trimmed back onto the old 60 budget (see the ability-score paragraph above). baseStats (maxHealth, speed, attack, physicalDefense, magicalDefense) were left untouched by that change on purpose — the point of moving abilities without touching baseStats is that a character's EFFECTIVE stats (Health, Attack, Speed, Mana Regen, both DEF lines, Max Mana) move on their own, purely through AbilityDerivation, with nothing hand-tuned to compensate. ROSTER ORDER IS FILE ORDER: sortOrder is assigned from position here, because Resources.LoadAll returns filename order and that silently reshuffles which characters land in the default squad (CLAUDE.md gotcha 4). Three of the five CharacterRole values are covered by the shipped roster (Utility, Tank, Support); Assassin and CrowdControl are unclaimed, for whichever character ships next. plateArt is the character's OWN FIGHT-HUD PLATE -- the wide leather strip with their head embossed at the right end, which the fight column draws their name, meters and status badges on. Resources-relative and without an extension like the two art paths above, REQUIRED on every row, and refused at build time if the file loads nothing: the acting character is a highlight on their own plate now rather than a promotion to a bigger card, so a row without a plate has no face in the HUD at all. tools/normalize_pc_plates.py is what produces the file (it brings the owner's three separately-drawn strips to one canvas and one aspect) and docs/ART_PIPELINE.md section 1 registers the kit. plateTheme is the character's IDENTITY COLOUR, worn by the rim and the name of every fight-HUD card that stands for them (Domain.UiKit.PcTheme maps the theme to its two hexes); matched case-insensitively against UiKit.ButtonTheme and REQUIRED on every row -- an empty or unknown value refuses the build, because every valid value is some other character's colour. Field-by-field documentation, defaults and valid enum values: docs/CONTENT_SCHEMA.md.
